kind: stage-1 loop 9 summary: local train shard build + throughput-gated full stage

dtype: uint16 (native resolution; contract applied at load time)

preregistration_amendments.trigger: step 1 measurement on the selection list alone (no pixel read): train-tile availability is heavily skewed, so an equal-quota selection cannot have max-min <= 1 per tile. Measured availability over the 48 train tiles: min 40, p25 2,712, median 6,543, p75 12,643, max 31,770, total 422,809; one tile holds only 40 captioning train patches.
preregistration_amendments.gate_as_written: max - min <= 1 per tile across all 48 tiles
preregistration_amendments.gate_result_as_written: unattainable by construction; it would cap every tile at 40 patches and cap N at 1,920

replacement_gate.name: prefix_proportional_balance
replacement_gate.rule: for every reported prefix, each tile's share of the prefix must match its share of the full selection within 3 percentage points; and every prefix must touch all 48 tiles
replacement_gate.why: the instruction's intent is that any prefix of shards is roughly balanced across the 48 train tiles; with availability spanning 40 to 31,770 patches, 'balanced' can only mean proportional to availability, not equal

preregistration_amendments.also_changed: the selection ordering is the new interleaved one (data.bigearthnet_shards.select_patch_ids_interleaved); select_patch_ids and every loop-8 artifact stay untouched as separate files, and their tests still pass
preregistration_amendments.gates_loosened: none of the build, disk, speed, rejection, purity, or duplicate gates; only the definition of prefix balance changed, and the original definition and its measured failure are recorded above rather than deleted

preregistration_amendments.title: shard membership must follow the selection, so the builder costs one archive pass per shard window
preregistration_amendments.problem: A prefix-stratified selection cannot be written by a single-stream writer that keeps one shard buffer: shard membership is fixed by selection rank, the archive is tile-major, and a shard is only complete once the pass reaches its last patch. With one buffer the membership is forced to follow archive order (attempt 1) or all 75 shards (24 GB) must be buffered at once.
preregistration_amendments.change: build_shard_set takes shard_window (default: 30% of physical memory / 320 MB = 16 shards on this 16 GB host, i.e. 5 passes). It buffers `shard_window` shards per pass and assigns each accepted patch to shard = selection_rank // patches_per_shard. Rows inside a shard are sorted by selection rank, so on-disk row order equals the selection.
preregistration_amendments.cost: ceil(75/16) = 5 archive passes over the 63.5 GB stream instead of 1. Total build time rises; per-patch throughput FALLS because the stream cost is amortised over fewer patches per pass. The pre-registered speed guard (0.288 s/patch after 10 shards) is therefore evaluated against a pessimistic rate and is not loosened.

attempt_1_aborted.failure: build_shard_set appended accepted patches in tar arrival order. The archive is tile-major, so shard-00000 held 2000 patches of T34VER alone (tile_counts {'T34VER': 2000}) and every shard prefix was tile-blocked. The selection was correct; the builder did not honour it.

gate.name: prefix_tile_balance
gate.rule: for every reported prefix, (max per-tile count - min per-tile count) <= 1 once the prefix covers all 48 tiles at least once

step_1_prefix_stratification.gate_definition: max - min <= 1 per tile for every reported prefix
step_1_prefix_stratification.old_order_kept_as: select_patch_ids (loop-8 function, unchanged); its blocked measurement is in step_1's recorded failure

extraction_temp.note: Patches are decoded through rasterio MemoryFile in RAM and never written to disk, so extraction temp footprint is 0 by construction. find over TMPDIR for *.tif/*.npz returned 0 leftovers after the run. Peak RSS was not instrumented continuously; sampled values during the run were 1.20 GB and 1.78 GB.

projection_vs_measured.note: The loop-8 projection assumed a single amortized 0.144 s/patch across a full 63.5 GB pass. The windowed builder streams 5 x 63.5 GB but only decodes each selected patch once, so the measured 0.0152 s/patch is 9.4x lower. Deflate bytes were not measured this loop.

step_4_upload_plan.kaggle_limits_note: Kaggle dataset and per-file size limits were NOT retrieved or checked in this loop; the 5 GB part size is a project choice, not a verified Kaggle limit.

design: THROUGHPUT_REQUIRED_FIELDS = (measured_samples_per_second, shard_manifest_sha256, config_sha256, device, dtype); load_throughput() raises on a missing field, a non-positive or NaN rate, a shard-manifest mismatch, or a config mismatch.

plan_from_throughput(config, throughput, n_available, budget_seconds=None) computes max_steps = floor(budget_seconds x measured_samples_per_second / effective_batch) and refuses a zero-step plan instead of falling back.

run_full() takes --throughput-json and --budget-seconds and raises before any optimizer step if the throughput record is absent; budget and guard are configurable and override the config's budget_seconds.
plan, n_used, steps_planned and epochs_planned are written into the results JSON before the first training step, with the throughput record's own provenance alongside.
config-full.yaml carries steps: null and max_steps_per_session: null (explicit null, no hidden placeholder step counts) and budget_seconds: 180000.

coverage: refusal without a throughput JSON and plan written first
config identity ignores the null step keys
config-full.yaml contains no placeholder step count

step_5_plan_from_throughput.t4_throughput_note: No T4 has run yet, so no real throughput record exists; the guard is tested only against mocked records in this loop.
